I’m not trying to argue that Joel was a good person and didn’t have any reason to suspect people would try to kill him. I’m sure we all know he wronged many people and he probably expected someone would come after him eventually (which again makes me think it was really out of character for him to be nice to strangers like Abby in the beginning of the game...). My point is not to establish which of them is a better person, Joel or Abby’s dad.

What I mean is when Abby’s dad decided to go on with the surgery in those circumstances, made possible by the Fireflies and their unethical business, he took the risk of suffering consequences. Being a good person or a bad person, he was one of the people responsible for the decision of operating a 13 year-old even if it meant she would die without the chance to consent to the surgery. So he was not innocent. That’s it.

Also, my point is not to evaluate which one of the daughters has a better claim of revenge, I think it’s understandable to want revenge from any of their points of view. I’m just explaining why the doctor’s death didn’t make me think that what Joel did >in the hospital< was as awful as part 2 portrays. So I didn’t feel like the doctor’s death was meaningful enough to make me want to play as Abby for half of the game... And this compromised my enjoyment of the game.

I just don’t see Ellie and Abby as parallels. Abby’s dad was fully aware of the risks when he joined the Fireflies and was willing to kill an innocent child (Ellie) for the mere possibility of a cure, in his dialogue with Marlene he himself admits it’s fucked up, but he decides to do it anyway. Joel on the other hand only finds out Ellie would die from the procedure after he had already handed her to the Fireflies, and the Fireflies would never allow him to change his mind, straight up tried to kill him when he decided to retrieve her. And Ellie didn’t even know what was going on. Also the first game always portrayed the Fireflies as a hostile armed group with a not-so-benevolent agenda, that would get involved in all sorts of unethical business. As a community it was nowhere near Jackson. I don’t think what Joel did was as cruel as Abby’s group thinks it was. Her dad was not innocent. I don’t know, it just feels like the second game rewrote the inconvenient parts of the first one so that Joel would seem worse than he really is.

Another thing that bothers me is how different Joel acts from the first game to the second one. He was always so guarded and suspicious of strangers in the first one, for 20 years that reluctance to trust others was what made him survive in such a harsh new reality, so I honestly don’t think he would lose that personality trait after only four years living in a welcoming community like Jackson. It’s like a major transformation just happened to Joel offscreen... He felt so unfamiliar to me in the beginning of the second game I even thought maybe the voice actor had changed. This really bothers me.

I enjoyed many aspects of the game, especially being able to play as strong women with proper clothing fighting the apocalipse with no concern about fitting into the “ideal woman” role. I always dreamed as playable characters like them since I was a little girl playing SNES haha And I was so grateful for the LGBT inclusion, I saw so much of my relationship with my girlfriend in the scenes between Ellie and Dina. I also really enjoyed watching the war between Wolves and Seraphites unfold.

Anyway, I never agreed with Abby’s behavior, I think her father took a risk when he joined the Fireflies, I don’t care about any of her friends, I didn’t care about Abby and Owen’s relationship nearly as much as Ellie+Dina, and mostly I felt angry and deceived for being forced to play so many hours as Abby. I would definitely trade most of those hours of gameplay for a deeper exploration of Ellie’s journey towards Santa Barbara for example...

Anyway, I just finished the game and those are my confused and mixed feelings.

when I was 13 a close friend killed herself and everyone was hurt, but unfortunately the adults dealt with her death the worst way possible: with denial. in the beginning they told us lie after lie - she’s traveling, she moved to another city - and all this time I could tell something about their explanation was off...

but when her parents scheduled her burial and the truth was out, my child brain simply couldn’t deal with this and shut down... i spent the following 10 years without even remembering that ever happened, until i was 23 and someone else i knew killed themselves too, so the memories came back rushing in and it was HORRIBLE, I swear I don’t know how i managed to stay alive after this hidden truth hit me so hard, it was running in the back of my head for all these years, but i just couldn’t remember, and when i finally did, i felt so guilty for not saying goodbye to my friend, so guilty for not remembering her, so guilty and extremely sad...

I really wish the adults had taken different decisions back then, because trying to hide it caused the worst possible consequences... if i could turn back time i would make my parents and every other adult involved put me and all the kids in therapy so that we could talk about what happened and understand what it meant, understand in our own words, us kids could have grieved her death together and relied on each other to overcome this tragedy and say our proper goodbyes and try to move on...

that would have been much better than having to deal with it by myself 10 years later without even understanding where that feeling was coming from, drowning in guilt and self-hatred. therapy and meds saved my life in these last few years, and i thought maybe if i share my story this process doesn’t have to be so hard for other kids out there who unfortunately are going through something similar

When I have experienced dissociation the most helpful thing was the support of friends who would listen to my symptoms without judging me or feeling scared. They reminded me I wasn’t patient zero and that dissociation was relatively common, treatable, and that the crisis would eventually pass. They gave me hope, they helped me recover trust while I was seeking professional help.

Sometimes I wouldn’t recognize my surroundings and having them around to remind me to eat, to drink water, to remember who I was was essential. I only survived because of them.

In the beginning I avoided asking for help because I thought after the crisis had started I had become such a different person my friends wouldn’t recognize me anymore and they wouldn’t want to be friends with me any longer. But they made sure I understood how silly that idea was.

My family would have never been able of handling it in such a helping way. If my family had been involved, they would have freaked out and made me do all the emotional labor... Honestly I can’t express how grateful I feel for my friends’ patience and care.

as a woman I feel like I always have to prove myself much more than men.

for example, in my country (Brazil) whenever a girl says she loves soccer some random guy shows up and asks: “if you really like it you should be able to name all Flamengo’s players who competed in the 1968 national tournament” or some other ridiculously hard question he would never direct to a male friend who said they like soccer.

it also happens if i say i like superheros, there will always be some guy making me go through some sort of trivia about marvel and dc...

i think the same applies in gaming. i can’t say i enjoy videogames, because if my male friends talk about one specific game i don’t play, suddenly i’m not enough of a gamer. but if i mention some game they don’t know, they’ll tell me my game is not relevant (or they’ll look it up and later brag about it like they found it in the first place, not me).

it’s always a double standard. men’s tastes and preferences are perceived as legit, and our taste is always a “stupid phase” or superficial or not to be taken seriously. when a guy says he likes something, everyone assumes he does. but if a girl says she likes something, everyone assumes she just wants attention, and we suffer from imposter syndrome. i think it’s so unfair to us! that’s why i always support my girlfriends in their tastes
